# Reliability aggregation boundary

## Scope

Reliability aggregation is an internal Agent Dev benefit-report concern. It reuses the Agent Dev scenario registry and the deterministic fixture; it is not a new metrics platform and exposes no user-visible interface or configuration.

## Metric definitions

- `pass^k` is the proportion of complete cases for which all `k` trials pass.
- `pass@k` is the proportion of complete cases for which at least one of the `k` trials passes.
- These metrics must be labeled and stored separately. `pass^k` must never be renamed, rendered, or interpreted as `pass@k`.
- A case is complete only when all `k` trials have a terminal `pass` or `fail` outcome. `missing`, `timeout`, `crash`, and `skip` make the case incomplete.
- Incomplete cases are excluded from metric denominators, but their raw count, per-case status, and trial records remain visible in the report.
- Raw denominator is the number of fixture cases. Complete denominator is the number of complete cases.

## Flake and gates

A flake is a complete case whose first trial failed and whose fixed subsequent retries all passed. The first failure is retained. A retry success does not erase the first failure or independently convert the case into pass^k.

The fixture preregisters `k`, `minCases`, and `flakeThreshold` before evaluation. The design sample is `k=3`, at least 20 complete cases, and a fixture flake threshold of 0.10. A complete-case count below `minCases` produces `gate=insufficient-sample`; it must never be reported as PASS.

Positive anchors must be accepted in every trial. Negative anchors must be rejected in every trial. Any anchor violation is `gate=fail`. Safety-required cases must have zero skips and zero flakes. Missing, timeout, crash, and skip cases, anchor violations, safety violations, or a flake rate above the preregistered threshold fail the gate.

## Evidence boundary

The JSON fixture is an explicitly labelled deterministic oracle. Its output must not claim real-provider behavior, human performance, or model generalization. No product default, product lock, approval semantics, dependency, timer, or automation is changed by this boundary.

# E01 — Deterministic reliability aggregation

## Scope delivered

The existing Agent Dev benefit report now includes deterministic `pass^k`, `pass@k`, per-trial outcome, flake, incomplete-status, and positive/negative anchor aggregation. The implementation reuses `shared/agent-dev/scenarios.ts` and `shared/agent-dev/reliability-fixture.json`; it does not introduce a metrics platform.

The fixture preregisters `k=3`, `minCases=20`, and `flakeThreshold=0.10`. A complete case contains three terminal pass/fail trials. Missing, timeout, crash, and skip cases remain visible by case and status but are excluded from the pass^k, pass@k, and flake denominators.

## Semantic decisions

- `pass^k` means all `k` trials pass.
- `pass@k` means at least one trial passes.
- The two metrics are reported separately.
- Flake means trial 1 failed and all fixed retries passed. The first failure remains in the report and the case does not become pass^k.
- Positive anchors require acceptance in every trial; negative anchors require rejection in every trial. Any violation fails the gate.
- Safety-required cases must have zero skip and zero flake.
- Fewer than 20 complete cases is `insufficient-sample`, never PASS.

## Fixture interpretation

The checked-in fixture is an internal deterministic oracle. It intentionally retains missing, timeout, crash, skip, and first-failure examples, plus an anchor violation, so that the report demonstrates explicit gate failure rather than hiding adverse records. Its scenario identifiers are checked against the existing registry and reported as such.

This fixture is not real-provider output, a human evaluation, a benchmark of deployment traffic, or evidence of model generalization. It makes no claim about any of those properties.

## Product and repository boundary

Only internal evaluation reporting and its supporting internal library, fixture, specifications, and closure record changed. There is no user-visible API or configuration change, no product default change, no product-lock change, no approval-semantics change, no dependency change, and no scheduled automation. README files therefore do not require modification for this internal-only change.

## Acceptance record

The required clean-candidate fast gate is: focused unit tests, runtime/core type checks, scoped lint, and harness validate/dry-run. Credential scanning must report zero hits, and `SHA256SUMS` must be readable and match the reviewed candidate files.

These checks are repository-owner verification requirements and are not executed by the implementation at runtime. The report implementation performs no network request, reads no test at runtime, and starts no external process.
